$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.
goal: fix the three medium findings (from run 2026-10-18-orchestra-p3b-desktop-pairing review: (1) link_config::load accepts any port, so a hand-edited config.json with port 0 or below MIN_PORT auto-starts on a random/low port, against G7; (2) the initial link status snapshot can overwrite a newer link-status-changed event at startup; (3) the modals (PairingRequest, PairingDialog) do not keep keyboard focus inside - no Tab trap, background not inert)

Settings::default() uses DEFAULT_PORT at link_config.rs:36. The UI has its own copies at orchestra/desktop/src/link.ts:7 (MIN_PORT 1024) and link.ts:9 (DEFAULT_PORT 47800).

Q1 load() is orchestra/desktop/src-tauri/src/link_config.rs:61-79. The port is parsed only by serde: Settings.port is u16 (link_config.rs:25, struct deny_unknown_fields at :21), decoded at link_config.rs:75 via serde_json::from_value::<Settings>; a decode error maps to ReadOnly::Unreadable (link_config.rs:77). There is NO range check in load(): port 0 and port 22 decode as valid and return (settings, None) at link_config.rs:76. The status dispatch is unconditional and runs after the whole Promise.all resolves, so an event delivered during that await lands first and the stale snapshot overwrites it.

Q2 linkReducer status case, orchestra/desktop/src/link.ts:196-200: case "status": with a comment (A link that stopped has no request left to answer.), then const requests = action.status.running ? state.requests : []; and return { ...state, status: action.status, requests, pairing: action.status.running ? state.pairing : false }. No sequence check; it overwrites status unconditionally. link.test.ts:268-274 pins only the stopped-drops-requests behaviour.

Q2 the status payload is the Rust struct LinkStatus, link.rs:44-61: available, os, enabled, running, addrs, port, binds, missing, error, config_readonly, firewall_notice_seen. There is NO seq, revision, generation, timestamp or any orderable field. The only SystemTime use in link.rs is link.rs:179 (millis, used for pending expires_at), not status.

Q2 the event is emitted by emit_status() at link.rs:281-285: if let Ok(v) = serde_json::to_value(self.status()) then (self.emit)(EV_STATUS, v); with EV_STATUS = link-status-changed (link.rs:38). It is called as the last statement of apply() (link.rs:386). The link_status command at link.rs:558-561 is pub fn link_status(link: State<LinkRef>) -> LinkStatus { link.status() }, sync, returning the same struct. status() at link.rs:258-272 takes lock(&self.slot) and copies fields; no counter is read.

Q2 ordering facts that matter for the fix: apply() runs under the lifecycle mutex (auto_start thread link.rs:394-398; set_config holds the guard at link.rs:402), so status emits from apply are serialized in state order. Every status change in this module goes through apply() (set_config link.rs:426-427, auto_start link.rs:398). set_config early return (link.rs:421-423) changes nothing and emits nothing. So each state change emits one event after it mutates the slot, and emission order equals state order.

Q2 answer for the plan: a reducer rule (ignore the snapshot if any link-status-changed event has arrived) is sufficient for the race at App.tsx:75, under the facts above (every change emits after mutating; emit order equals state order; App.tsx:54 subscribes before App.tsx:71 reads). A snapshot that loses to a delivered event is older than that event, and any change after the read emits its own later event. Rust does not need a counter for this race. A LinkStatus generation or seq (bumped under the slot lock in apply, carried in the event and the command) would remove the reliance on delivery order, but Tauri cross-thread event delivery order is NOT verified in this tree (unknown).

risks: PLAN-SHAPE RISK (Q3): the suspicion is half right. Devices.tsx:134, LinkSettings.tsx:199 and TaskDetail.tsx:136 and :151 are inline role=alertdialog cards with no overlay (App.css:537 applies only to .overlay). A Tab trap or inert on the background would not fit them; they need focus-on-mount and Escape handling, if anything. A shared fix should be scoped to the two overlays (a Modal wrapper with overlay, focus-in, Tab cycle, focus restore and inert on siblings), with the inline cards handled as a separate small item. Fixing only the two pairing modals is not inconsistent in layout terms, but leaves the inline cards without focus-on-mount.

PORT RISK (Q1): load() accepts port 0 and port 22 today (link_config.rs:75-76), and apply() binds settings.port directly (link.rs:362). A hand-edited enabled config with port 0 starts on a random port every launch and reports port 0 in LinkStatus (link.rs:272). The only range guard, validate() (link_config.rs:198-200), never runs on disk input.

READ-ONLY TRAP (Q1): if load() marks a bad port ReadOnly::Unreadable, set_config refuses every change (link.rs:406-408) and the UI cannot fix the port; the owner must edit or delete config.json. Decide whether that is acceptable (it is the G6 rule) or whether a port-only error should be fixable in the UI.

The reducer-only fix is correct only under the ordering invariants in the facts; a test must pin the event-arrived-first then snapshot order, which link.test.ts does not do today.

architect.run_scope: orchestra only. Exactly the three medium findings. ROADMAP.md is in no slice (orchestrator, at close). No change to core/, protocol/, tauri.conf.json, capabilities/**, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, package.json, package-lock.json, vite.config.ts or App.css. No new dependencies.
architect.rationale: Single-loop, one branch, two slices built in order s1 then s2 by one builder loop. Only two pieces, so a diamond is not available (it needs 3+). The file sets are disjoint (s1: two Rust files plus CLAUDE.md; s2: TypeScript only) and no artifact flows between them, so there is no real edge; the order only keeps one loop. CLAUDE.md is in s1 alone: only the shell test count at orchestra/CLAUDE.md:41 ('41 shell') changes, and no vitest count is written in CLAUDE.md (grep '206' finds none), so s2 needs no doc edit. Risk: s1 LOW - no secret or sensitive data, no file shared with s2, and every behaviour it adds (refused at start, file untouched, fixable by a save) is visible to the new shell test; done_when plus a scope check is enough evidence. s2 HIGH - the Tab trap, inert background and focus restore are DOM behaviour that no test in this tree can see (no jsdom, G11), and PairingRequest is the user's trust decision whose Escape-means-reject rule must not move; only a reader and the owner's hand test can check those. Verified against 806c4c3, not trusted: load() has no range check (link_config.rs:61-79; port is u16, so 70000 fails only at decode); validate() is the only range check (link_config.rs:198-200) and runs only from set_config; apply() binds settings.port as is (link.rs:362) and is gated only on enabled and read_only (link.rs:343); set_config refuses everything while read_only is Some (link.rs:406-408); LinkSettings shows status.error with Retry and an editable port field locked only by config_readonly or !available (LinkSettings.tsx:51, :148-151, :185-189). emit_status has exactly one caller, the last line of apply() (link.rs:386); apply's callers hold lifecycle (auto_start link.rs:394-398, set_config link.rs:402); status() takes only the slot lock (link.rs:258). App.tsx:54 subscribes before the Promise.all at :65-73 and dispatches the snapshot at :75 as an ordinary 'status' action; App.tsx:106 also dispatches set_config results as 'status'. The reducer keeps the two overlays mutually exclusive (link.ts:203 'request' clears pairing; :209 'pairing' opens only with no requests); App.tsx:196-205 renders both as children of div.app beside the header and main. Both components focus the dialog on mount and handle Escape on a window keydown listener (PairingRequest.tsx:71-78, PairingDialog.tsx:46-53). No disagreement with the scout's facts.

decisions_for_gate.title: A port outside 1024-65535 in config.json
decisions_for_gate.recommend: (b), implemented as a start error, not a new read-only kind. load() is unchanged and still returns the parsed settings with read_only None. A new pure helper link_config::port_error(port: u32) -> Option<String> holds the 1024..=65535 rule; validate() calls it (same message as today) and apply() calls it before split_binds when settings.enabled && read_only.is_none(): an out-of-range port sets slot.error to 'Port N is not allowed. Pick a port from 1024 to 65535 and Save.' and starts nothing. So an enabled file with port 0, 22 or 1023 auto-starts into: link off, enabled kept as saved, the file left byte-for-byte alone, settings editable, the error shown next to the port field (which already shows the bad value with aria-invalid via parsePort). Saving a valid port goes through validate and overwrites the file. Why this keeps G6 and G7: G6's read-only rule protects a file this build cannot fully understand (newer schema, unparseable), where a save would destroy data; a low port is a fully understood file with one bad value, and nothing is rewritten without the user's own Save. G6 already says 'A start error leaves the link off, keeps enabled as saved, and shows the error with Retry', and G7 already treats a busy port as 'a start error naming the port, with the port field next to it'; a forbidden port is the same case. G7's 'never 0' holds because nothing binds it. No UI code changes: the message is status.error, which LinkSettings.tsx:185-189 already renders. Retry with the bad port is refused by validate with 'the port must be between 1024 and 65535'; the user edits the field instead.
alternatives: (a) Fail closed as ReadOnly::Unreadable in load(), as port 70000 does today: one line and the strictest reading, but the settings become read-only (link.rs:406-408) and the only way out is a hand edit or delete of config.json, for a file whose every other field is valid. It would also need a UI message naming the file, since 'could not be read' is misleading for a readable file. Rejected as a worse user outcome for no safety gain: under (b) nothing binds either.
(c) Clamp to 47800 at load: contradicts fail-closed and silently starts the link on a port the user did not choose (and the QR then advertises it). Rejected.
decisions_for_gate.known_inconsistency: Port 70000 (any value over 65535) still fails at serde decode as Unreadable, read-only, because Settings.port is u16. Making it editable means decoding port as u32, a struct change beyond this finding. Left as is and named in NOT DOING.

decisions_for_gate.title: The startup snapshot must not overwrite a newer status event
decisions_for_gate.recommend: Pure reducer rule. LinkUi gains statusSeen: boolean (initialLinkUi false). Every existing 'status' action (the link-status-changed event at App.tsx:54 and set_config results at App.tsx:106) sets statusSeen true. A new action { type: 'snapshot'; status } is applied exactly like 'status' (same running-drops-requests and pairing rule) only when statusSeen is false, and returns the same state otherwise. App.tsx:75 dispatches 'snapshot' instead of 'status'. Rust needs no generation counter: emit_status() has one caller, the end of apply() (link.rs:386), and apply() always runs with lifecycle held (auto_start link.rs:394-398, set_config link.rs:402), after it has written the slot (link.rs:378-384). So the events form one serialized sequence in state order, and the subscription (App.tsx:54) is in place before link_status is read (App.tsx:71). A snapshot that loses to a delivered event is no newer than the last state that will be delivered: if it was read after mutation N, event N is emitted after that mutation and is either already delivered or still coming. The remaining assumption is that Tauri delivers serialized emits to the webview in emit order; not verified in this tree (scout unknown). A counter would carry a seq through LinkStatus, the ipc.ts decoder and types.ts: three more files and a DTO change for a narrow race.
alternatives: Generation counter in LinkStatus (bumped under the slot lock in apply, compared in the reducer): removes the delivery-order assumption, but changes the DTO, the decoder and its tests. Offer later if the race is ever seen with the rule in place.
Fetch linkStatus() in its own step after subscribing, outside the Promise.all: narrows the window but does not close it (an event can still arrive while the command is in flight). Rejected.
decisions_for_gate.tests: orchestra/desktop/src/link.test.ts, in the existing describe block for linkReducer: (1) "a status event that arrived first beats the startup snapshot": from initialLinkUi apply status(running:true) then snapshot(running:false) -> status.running is true and requests are kept. (2) "the startup snapshot applies when no event came first": from initialLinkUi apply snapshot(s) -> status equals s and statusSeen stays false; a later status(t) replaces it. (3) "a set_config result counts as seen": a status action then a snapshot leaves the status from the status action.

decisions_for_gate.title: Focus inside the two overlays
decisions_for_gate.recommend: One small shared module, orchestra/desktop/src/focus.ts. First, a pure export cycleFocus(count: number, current: number, back: boolean): number giving the index to focus on Tab (back false) or Shift+Tab (back true): -1 when count is 0; from current -1 (the dialog itself has focus, or focus is outside the list) Tab goes to 0 and Shift+Tab to count-1; otherwise wrap at both ends. Second, a hook useModalFocus(ref: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>) used by both overlays, mount-only (empty deps): on mount it records document.activeElement as the opener, focuses ref.current, and sets inert on every sibling of the overlay element (ref.current.parentElement, the div.overlay) inside its parent, recording only the siblings it changed; it adds a keydown listener on ref.current (not on window) that handles only Tab: it lists the enabled focusable descendants (button, input, select, textarea, [href], [tabindex] other than -1, excluding disabled), calls cycleFocus with the index of document.activeElement and e.shiftKey, then preventDefault and focuses that element (or the dialog itself when the list is empty). On unmount it removes the listener, clears inert on exactly the siblings it set, then focuses the opener if it is still connected. It never handles Escape and never calls stopPropagation, so Escape stays with the components' existing window listeners: PairingRequest Escape rejects, PairingDialog Escape closes, unchanged. PairingRequest.tsx and PairingDialog.tsx call useModalFocus(dialog) and drop the now-duplicate dialog.current?.focus() line from their Escape effects; nothing else in those effects changes. React runs all unmount cleanups of a commit before its new mount effects, so the QR-dialog-to-request hand-over (link.ts:203) restores, then re-traps.
alternatives: Native <dialog> with showModal(): top layer and an inert page for free, but the browser's own cancel-on-Escape closes the element behind React's back, so both components need a cancel handler with preventDefault and the two Escape paths become ambiguous, exactly the scout's same-key risk. It also moves the backdrop from .overlay to ::backdrop (App.css change) and relies on a WebView2 version not checked on the owner's machine. Rejected.
